title: Evaluation of T2 mapping after furosemide administration to determine side-by-side renal function in pediatric MR-urography
summary: Congenital malformations of the kidneys and urinary tract account for 20-30% of all anomalies identified prenatally. In 30-50% of children, these malformations can lead to chronic renal dysfunction and the need for renal replacement therapy. It is therefore important to diagnose these anomalies as early and accurately as possible in order to initiate treatment promptly and minimize kidney damage. Magnetic resonance urography (MRU) is a diagnostic imaging modality that uses contrast media. The administration of contrast agents, particularly those containing gadolinium, can be associated with risks, including the risk of gadolinium deposition in the brain and other organs and tissue damage to the kidney. The trial will test alternative MRI measurement techniques that may eliminate the need for gadolinium-based contrast agents.
conditions: Congenital malformations of the urinary system

interventions.name: Paediatric patients undergoing Magnetic Resonance Urography (MRU) with administration of furosemide and gadolinium-based contrast agent for clinical indications will receive measurement with additional MRI T2-mapping sequences integrated into the standard MRU procedure for study purposes.
Paediatric patients undergoing Magnetic Resonance Urography (MRU) with administration of furosemide and gadolinium-based contrast agent for clinical indications.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Male and female patients
- Pediatric referral with clinical indication for contrast-enhanced MRU with furosemide administration.
- Availability of all necessary laboratory parameters (creatinine/GFR according to internal guidelines of the UKT)
- Written informed consent from patient and/or guardian
Exclusion criteria:
- All MRI relevant exclusion criteria 
- All contrast media-related exclusions
- All Furosemid-related exclusions
- Non-compliance of patients to undergo an MRI scan. 
- No written consent to the study from the patient and/or guardian, or clear refusal from younger children (usually <12 years).
